## Historical audit: S0314

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H02/selection/bw_0031/1/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines; all cited observations are complete lines, not split fragments.

| Evidence | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| Goal: H request, line 1 | Reconstruct an indoor scene and viewpoint from a 374 × 512 reference, using separate editable meshes. The semantic goal was image fidelity, not merely a runnable scene. The reference image itself is not visible in this audit. |
| Initial build: H response/execute, lines 3–4 | H interpreted the input as a composite: a room photograph plus a separate yellow GRID panel whose physical room location was unknown. It nevertheless placed the panel on a room wall. Code emitted multiple named assets: architecture, instrument bank, sloping desk, doorway, small console and panel, with child controls. These names and groupings do not verify physical connections or reference completeness. |
| Appearance and pose: lines 3–4, 13–14, 23–24 | Code used colored surfaces and attempted emissive lamps; no texture mapping is evident. It specified desk slope, object positions, overview and detail cameras, world illumination and area lights. It also requested 1920 × 1080 render settings despite the portrait reference; the runner’s effective output dimensions are not established here. |
| Exploration: H responses, lines 13 and 23 | After receiving reference and render images, H reported first an exterior view with excessive empty space and hidden rear objects, then a still-obscured doorway and small console, nearly horizontal desk and washed-out controls. These are H’s visual assessments, not independent verification. H revised camera position/target/lens, asset dimensions and positions, desk outlines, colors and lighting; the revised complete programs were executed in lines 14 and 24. |
| Validation: execution results, lines 9, 19 and 29; selections, lines 10, 20 and 30 | All three builds and renders returned `ok: true`; step 3 was selected. Logs show 16 render samples although programs requested 32. This establishes technical execution, not geometric or visual correctness. No post-step-3 visual review or `DONE` is recorded. |
| Input and autonomy: H requests, lines 11 and 21; sessions, lines 2, 12 and 22 | The runner supplied comparison instructions and images after each of the first two renders; subsequent revisions show H acted on that feedback. No separate teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update or teacher-message receipt is visible. H sessions show no tool calls; its iterative exploration was through generated programs and runner feedback. |

**Outcome:** Three nonempty scene programs executed successfully and the last was selected. Final reconstruction quality is **unknown**, not formally verified success or an established algorithm failure. There is no observed technical interruption.

**Lessons and uncertainty:** The transferable pattern is to separate image-based discrepancy reports from executable changes and verify the resulting render; successful execution alone cannot establish fidelity. The panel’s real placement, actual part contact, texture fidelity, final framing and illumination remain unresolved. In particular, the hypothesis that camera and lighting changes fixed H’s reported defects was not tested by an observed final comparison. The panel-to-room integration is task-specific and explicitly speculative.
